transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I’m here because... I'm pretty sure the people on this environmental modeling contract I'm working on have been tracking my revisions. They've been deliberately planting errors in the datasets. 

It's obvious to me they're doing it to make it look like I can’t lead the work anymore. My wife keeps telling me, and the junior analysts at work too, they say it’s just, you know, routine version-control mistakes. But I know what I'm looking at, and I know they're tampering with it.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

No, I don't hear voices. I mean, I hear people talking when they're actually in the room with me, of course, but... no, not when I'm alone. I'm not hearing things. I'm just seeing what they're doing to the numbers in the datasets. It's all right there on the screen.
Have you been feeling unusually energetic or high lately?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel high or... overly energetic at all. 

If anything, I'm just tired. It takes a lot out of you, having to constantly comb through the models and double-check everything just to find the errors they keep slipping in. But as far as my actual energy goes, no, it's just normal. I haven't noticed any weird spikes or anything like that.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day?

No, I wouldn't say I've been depressed. I'm not sad or down, really. I mean, it's stressful, dealing with the project and feeling like I have to watch my back all the time. But it's not depression. I'm just focused on getting the work done and proving what they're doing.
How long have you been convinced that your coworkers are deliberately tampering with the datasets?

Well, let me think... it's been about two months. I might have had my suspicions a little before that when I first started noticing the anomalies in the numbers, but for the last two months, I've been absolutely certain. That's how long I've known for a fact that the people on the project are tracking my revisions and deliberately planting those errors.
Before this started, had you had any recent medical illness, head injury, seizure, or change in medications or drug use?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick... no head injuries or seizures, definitely not. And my medications are exactly the same. I don't use drugs, either. Physically, I've been perfectly fine.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

No, nobody's mentioned anything like that to me. I think I speak pretty clearly. I mean, my thoughts are organized, especially when I'm explaining the data or the errors I've found. I haven't had anyone tell me I'm hard to follow or jumping around.
Have you found yourself losing interest or motivation to do things you used to do?

Yeah, I suppose I have. These days, I can just sit for hours at my desk... or out in the garage with the telescope still covered up. I know I used to really enjoy hiking, mentoring the younger analysts at work, and going to astronomy nights. But lately, I just don't feel much pull to start anything, or even to talk to anyone, really.
Have you been talking much less than you used to?

Yes, like I was just saying, I really don't say much at all anymore. I just... I sit there at my desk, or out in the garage by the covered telescope, and I'm just quiet. I used to talk a lot more, especially when I was mentoring the younger analysts at work or chatting with people at those astronomy nights. But now, I just don't have the urge to hold a conversation with anyone.
Have you noticed your emotions feeling flatter than usual, like your face or voice shows less feeling even when something should move you?

I suppose so. It really just ties back into what I was just telling you. When I'm sitting there for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered up, I'm just... blank. I don't really feel much inside, so I guess it makes sense that my face and voice wouldn't show much either. Even if I think about the things that used to get me excited, like hiking, or mentoring the younger analysts, or going to those astronomy nights... there's just no reaction. I just don't feel that pull to express anything anymore.
Since this started, has your ability to do your job dropped noticeably?

Yeah, it definitely has. I've... well, I've fallen pretty far behind on my modeling deliverables at work. It got to the point where the firm actually had to reassign pieces of my contract to other people. And like I mentioned about the junior analysts I'm supposed to supervise... I've basically stopped being useful to them. 

It's not just at the office, either. At home, I mostly just keep to myself now. My wife has had to really push me lately just to keep basic routines going.
Did this change in you come on very suddenly, over a few days?
No, it wasn't sudden like that. It wasn't just a few days. It's been more of a... a slow slide, I guess. It took a while to get to this point.
